title: What If Earth Swapped Places With Venus?

scenes.text: What if Earth swapped places with Venus? You wouldn't have long.
Venus orbits at 0.72 astronomical units, so sunlight on Earth would be almost twice as strong.
Climate models put the runaway greenhouse limit near 0.97 astronomical units. Earth would be well inside it.
Oceans would evaporate into thick steam, and that water vapor would trap even more heat.
Venus shows where it ends: 467 degrees Celsius, and air pressure 93 times Earth's.
The twist: NASA says early Venus had oceans too. Distance from the Sun may be the whole difference.
